conviction_note: Abs move 17% (event-implied 16.0%, first formal FY27 guide due with this print, 8-print median 10.1% with Q1 guide prints at -54%); p_up 53, a slight up lean from positioning: short interest is 19.2% of shares with 10.5 days to cover and rising, upside is paid in the skew (-3.6), and an activist settled on Oct 8 with a capital-allocation committee and $311m of buyback authorisation left. Against that sit operating negatives management already disclosed: applications behind, the 12k-student Texas school closed, a new CEO giving his first guide, and a competitor gaining share. The findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is +1.0. Both are near zero; the sign is not established.
bar: Q1 FY27 (Sep-26 quarter): consensus EPS $1.30 and revenue $611.2M (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/LRN). A single-analyst aggregator shows revenue $647M and EPS $1.32 (TickFlow, https://www.tickflow.io/stock/LRN/forecast). EPS agrees across the two sources at about $1.30; revenue is DISPUTED by about 6%, so every revenue-based size is capped small. The company gave no Q1 or FY27 guide (Q4 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001157408/000117184326005202/exh_991.htm). The line the stock trades on is the first formal FY27 enrollment and financial guide, and no sourced FY27 consensus was found. Year-ago Q1 FY26: revenue $620.9M, enrollments 247.7K, revenue per enrollment $2,388.
positioning_check: Short interest 7,968,668 shares on 2026-09-30, 19.2% of 41.56M shares outstanding (higher as % of float), 10.45 days to cover, up from 6.64M / 16.0% on 2026-07-31 (Equibles FINRA table, https://equibles.com/stocks/lrn/shortinterest). The Oct-15 settlement is not out until 2026-10-26. Benzinga showed about 25.9% short float in mid-September (per sweep row). Skew_25d is -3.61 vol points, so upside is paid. Put/call OI is 0.63. ATM IV is 74%, event-implied move 16.0%. Spot is $80.62, 47% off the 52-week high, +2.45% over 20 days and -2.87% over 5 days. This is a crowded and growing short into a guide print with calls bid, so negatives are shrunk for squeeze risk.

findings.finding: On the Aug-4 Q4 call the CFO said Q1 count-date enrollment growth 'will face a more difficult comparison than it has for the last couple of years'. An analyst's arithmetic on the call put the count date at roughly flat, about -0.4% y/y. The CEO said applications are 'tracking slightly behind' while conversion and re-registration are higher. Revenue per enrollment is guided flat to up slightly for FY27 and gross margin 'flattish' to 37.8%. A flat enrollment count at the year-ago $2,388 per enrollment implies Q1 revenue of about $615-625M (FY26 Q1 $620.9M), roughly 1-2% above the $611.2M bar but below the $647M single-analyst figure. The quarter therefore looks in line, and the guide decides the move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on enrollment and the guide, not the quarter. In Aug-2026 a $0.48 EPS beat with a revenue beat moved +2.65%. Apr-2026 moved +2.79%. Oct-2025 (Q1 with the guide) moved -54% on enrollment and platform problems. Jan-2026 moved +14.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The call text has been public since August, and the $611M consensus already implies a slight y/y decline. If the market believed flat enrollment the revenue bar would sit nearer $620M; the disputed $647M shows estimates are not anchored. Capped small because the revenue bar is disputed and because a quarter landing inside guided commentary is not new.
findings.independence: Q4 FY26 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001157408/000117184326005202/exh_991.htm): Q4 enrollments -0.5% y/y, General Education revenue -9.7%, Career Learning enrollments +9.7%, Q4 adjusted operating income -9.8%. Same company, different document; the exit rate is soft but flat.

findings.finding: Lone Star Online Academy, about 12,000 students and about 5% of Stride's projected enrollment, closed in June 2026 when Roscoe Collegiate ISD did not renew. Stride offered families tuition-free places in its private Grand Canyon Preparatory Academy (normally $7,500), and it cannot fit all students into its three public Texas schools under state transfer rules. That is a headwind to the FY27 enrollment and revenue-per-enrollment guide: retained students moving to waived-tuition private seats add enrollment without revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Contract losses have hit this stock before: the 2025-10-28 Q1 print fell 54% on lost enrollments, though that was platform-driven. The Lone Star news itself (June 2026) predates the baseline's reaction set.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public since June and discussed on the Q4 call. What is not visible is how many of the 12k Stride retained, and at what revenue, which only the FY27 guide reveals. A fully priced loss would show no residual put demand, and the skew is in fact call-leaning. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Q4 call: CFO 'we certainly had some performance issues with that school' and 'in any given year, we could have schools that do not decide to renew' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945508). The same company spoke on it, so this is not a fully independent source.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08 Stride signed a cooperation agreement with activist Fivespan Partners, about $1bn AUM, run by ex-ValueAct partner Dylan Haggart. Haggart joins the board on Oct 30 and co-chairs a new Capital Allocation Committee. Fivespan withdrew its nominations, proposal and Section 220 books-and-records demand. A target capital structure and cash-flow framework are due in about 3 months. Separately, $311.3M of buyback authorisation remains, about 9% of the $3.35bn market cap, and the CEO said on the Q4 call he intends opportunistic repurchases once the window opens at the end of October. FY26 free cash flow was $355M. Inside the window this is a floor under the stock, plus the chance the release or call signals buyback acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stride bought back about $100M in Q4 FY26 and $188.7M in FY26. No prior print turned on a buyback. The stock rose about 5% in the week after the Oct-9 announcement and has since given back about 3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 8-K is public and the stock reacted. Not priced is whether management uses its first post-activist print to announce an ASR or a larger authorisation. If the market expected that, short interest would be falling, but it rose to 19% through September. The framework itself is dated outside the window.
findings.independence: CEO on the Q4 call: 'Once our trading window opens at the end of October, I intend to actively consider opportunistic stock repurchases' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2945508). Repurchase authorisation and FY26 buyback from the Q4 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001157408/000117184326005202/exh_991.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 16.0% of shares (Jul-31) to 19.2% (Sep-30, 7.97M shares, 10.45 days to cover), with options skew_25d at -3.6 (upside paid) going into a first formal guide. Any guide that is not a clear enrollment decline forces covering into a 626k-share average day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Squeeze-shaped moves on this name: Jan-2026 +14.25% and Aug-2025 +15.67% on in-line-to-good prints. The downside is also violent (Oct-2025 -54%).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fact the price absorbs: shorts are paying to hold the view. It matters only as an asymmetry in the reaction to an in-line guide. If the short case were exhausted, short interest would be falling; it rose 20% in two months.
findings.independence: Baseline skew_25d -3.61 and put/call OI 0.63 (sealed baseline). The sweep row cites Benzinga at about 25.9% short float in mid-September (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LRN/sentiment).

findings.finding: Competitor Pearson Virtual Learning (Connections Academy) reported 2025/26 enrolment growth accelerating to 15% in the Spring semester, 'targeted marketing investment', 10 of 10 contract renewals and 5 new schools for 2026/27 (46 schools in 32 states). Over the same year Stride's General Education enrollments fell about 5% and General Education revenue fell 2.1% (Q4 -9.7%). The competitor is taking share in the segment that is 56% of Stride revenue, a headwind for the FY27 General Education guide. Net of the rest: Career Learning (44% of revenue, enrollments +9.7% in Q4) would have to keep growing high single digits to offset, and it has been doing so.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: General Education weakness was visible at the Apr-2026 (+2.79%) and Aug-2026 (+2.65%) prints and the stock still rose, so the market has looked through it twice.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer read-through from July, mostly priced. Strong industry demand (+) offsets share loss (-). Pearson's 2026/27 enrolment number comes on Oct 22, after this window. Filed small as a proxy and shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Proxy. Stride's own Q4 release shows General Education revenue -9.7% in Q4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001157408/000117184326005202/exh_991.htm).

findings.finding: This is the first formal guide under CEO Robert Knowling, appointed 2026-07-29 in an abrupt board-led change that cut the stock 15% intraday on 2026-07-30 alongside a William Blair downgrade. New CEOs commonly set a conservative first guide, which lands on the FY27 enrollment and operating-income range that decides this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-30 CEO-change day: -14.98% (baseline). Q1 guide prints: Oct-2025 -54% on a weak enrollment outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: The CEO change is priced; what is not knowable is how conservative the first guide will be. Inference, not a document, so filed small. Shrunk for squeeze risk and because the call skew argues the option market leans the other way.
findings.independence: Quiver Quant attributed the 7/30 selloff to the CEO succession and the downgrade (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Stride+shares+tumble+after+abrupt+CEO+transition+and+preliminary+FY2026+update). Same event, so not independent of the source.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the skew (upside paid) and with the crowded short only weakly. The operating evidence (weak applications, Lone Star, new CEO, competitor share gain) points the other way and is already public, so the net is close to zero and the move size, not the direction, is the content.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the revenue bar is disputed ($611M vs a single-analyst $647M), so the reported-quarter finding was capped from +0.5 to +0.3 and print_vs_bar cut from +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 7: a crowded short (19.2% of shares, 10.5 days to cover) plus a call-leaning skew shrank every negative: Lone Star -0.5 to -0.3, Pearson -0.5 to -0.3, new-CEO conservative guide -1.0 to -0.7.
Rule 3: the activist finding's own caveat (stock already rose about 5%; the framework comes in about 3 months) cut it from +1.0 to +0.7, and the framework moved to outside_window.
Rule 5 (positioning does not file as an unexplained drawdown) trimmed the positioning finding from +1.0 to +0.8 rather than dropping it, per the core's filing rule.
The net sum is unchanged at +0.5 because the cuts offset. p_up 53 and abs_move 17 were left standing.
